dishes.name: Beef Noodle Soup
dishes.desc: Braised beef shank in a rich soy or clear broth with wheat noodles, pickled mustard greens and scallions.

dishes.name: Bubble Tea
dishes.desc: Sweetened milk or fruit tea shaken with ice and served with chewy tapioca pearls, invented in Taichung in the 1980s.

dishes.name: Gua Bao
dishes.desc: Folded steamed bun filled with braised pork belly, pickled mustard greens, crushed peanuts and coriander.

dishes.name: Oyster Omelette
dishes.desc: Small oysters fried with egg and sweet potato starch batter, topped with a sweet and tangy red sauce at night markets.

dishes.name: Stinky Tofu
dishes.desc: Fermented tofu with a pungent smell, usually deep-fried and served with pickled cabbage and chili sauce at night markets.

dishes.name: Lu Rou Fan
dishes.desc: Rice topped with finely chopped pork belly braised in soy sauce, rice wine and five-spice, often with a braised egg.

dishes.name: Pineapple Cake
dishes.desc: Buttery shortbread pastry filled with sweet pineapple jam, a classic Taiwanese gift and souvenir.

dishes.name: Salt and Pepper Chicken
dishes.desc: Bite-sized marinated chicken pieces deep-fried with basil leaves and seasoned with salt, white pepper and chili powder.

dishes.name: Scallion Pancake
dishes.desc: Flaky unleavened flatbread folded with chopped scallions and oil, pan-fried until crisp and chewy.

dishes.name: Danzai Noodles
dishes.desc: Small bowl of noodles in shrimp broth topped with minced pork sauce, garlic and a shrimp, originating in Tainan.

dishes.name: Taiwanese Sausage
dishes.desc: Sweet, slightly fatty grilled pork sausage, often eaten with a raw garlic clove or inside a sticky-rice sausage at night markets.

dishes.name: Mango Shaved Ice
dishes.desc: Mound of finely shaved ice topped with fresh mango cubes, mango syrup, condensed milk and sometimes mango sorbet.

dishes.name: Three Cup Chicken
dishes.desc: Chicken braised in a clay pot with sesame oil, rice wine and soy sauce, finished with ginger, garlic and Thai basil.

dishes.name: Taiwanese Fried Chicken Cutlet
dishes.desc: Large flattened chicken breast marinated, coated in sweet potato flour and deep-fried, seasoned with pepper salt at night markets.

dishes.name: Tea Eggs
dishes.desc: Hard-boiled eggs simmered with cracked shells in black tea, soy sauce and spices, sold in convenience stores and stalls.

dishes.name: Night Market Grilled Squid
dishes.desc: Whole squid brushed with sweet soy glaze and grilled over charcoal on skewers, sold at Taiwanese night market stalls.

dishes.name: Turkey Rice
dishes.desc: Steamed rice topped with shredded turkey meat, turkey fat and shallot oil and soy sauce, a speciality of Chiayi.

dishes.name: Fan Tuan
dishes.desc: Glutinous rice rolled around a fried dough stick, pickled radish, pork floss and egg, eaten as a portable breakfast.

dishes.name: Dan Bing
dishes.desc: Thin chewy crepe fried with egg and rolled, often with cheese, corn or ham, sold at breakfast shops with soy paste.

dishes.name: Sun Cake
dishes.desc: Flaky round pastry filled with maltose syrup, a speciality of Taichung often bought as a souvenir.

dishes.name: Oyster Vermicelli
dishes.desc: Thin wheat vermicelli in thick starchy bonito broth with oysters or braised pig intestine, garlic and coriander.

dishes.name: Ba-wan
dishes.desc: Large translucent dumpling of sweet potato and rice starch filled with pork, bamboo shoots and mushrooms, served with sweet sauce.

dishes.name: Mongolian BBQ
dishes.desc: Diners choose raw meats and vegetables that are stir-fried on a large round iron griddle, a format created in Taipei in 1951.

dishes.name: Pepper Bun
dishes.desc: Peppery pork and scallion buns baked against the walls of a clay oven at night markets.

dishes.name: Aiyu Jelly
dishes.desc: Jelly set from fig seeds, served with lemon juice and honey over ice.

dishes.name: Lu Wei
dishes.desc: Tofu, eggs, offal and vegetables braised in a soy master stock, picked from a basket.

dishes.name: Douhua
dishes.desc: Silky tofu pudding with ginger syrup, peanuts and tapioca pearls.

dishes.name: High Mountain Oolong
dishes.desc: Oolong tea grown above 1,000 metres in Alishan and Lishan, floral and creamy.

dishes.name: Egg Waffle (Gai Daan Jai)
dishes.desc: Bubble-shaped waffle of sweet egg batter cooked on a special griddle and eaten warm from street stalls.

dishes.name: Milk Tea (Hong Kong)
dishes.desc: Strong black tea strained through a cloth "stocking" and mixed with evaporated or condensed milk, served in cha chaan teng.

dishes.name: Yuenyeung
dishes.desc: Mix of coffee and Hong Kong-style milk tea, served hot or iced in cha chaan teng cafés.

dishes.name: Wonton Noodles (HK)
dishes.desc: Thin springy egg noodles with shrimp wontons in a clear broth of dried flounder and pork bones, served in small bowls.

dishes.name: Pineapple Bun with Butter
dishes.desc: Sweet bun with a crackly sugar crust, split warm and filled with a thick slab of cold butter (bolo yau).

dishes.name: Fish Balls
dishes.desc: Springy balls of pounded fish paste, boiled in noodle soups or skewered and sold at street stalls.

dishes.name: Egg Tart (HK)
dishes.desc: Tart of shortcrust or flaky puff pastry filled with smooth egg custard, sold at bakeries and cha chaan teng.

dishes.name: Portuguese Egg Tart (Macau)
dishes.desc: Puff pastry tart with a caramelised, blistered custard top, popularised in Macau by Lord Stow's Bakery in 1989.

dishes.name: Macanese Pork Chop Bun
dishes.desc: Crusty bun filled with a marinated, fried bone-in pork chop, a classic Macau snack.

dishes.name: African Chicken (Macau)
dishes.desc: Grilled chicken in a spicy sauce of chili, coconut, peanuts and peppers, a Macanese dish with Portuguese-African roots.

dishes.name: Claypot Rice (HK)
dishes.desc: Rice cooked in a clay pot with toppings like Chinese sausage or chicken until a crispy crust forms, a winter favourite.

dishes.name: Siu Mei
dishes.desc: Cantonese roast meats such as char siu, roast goose and crispy pork belly, served over rice or sliced on platters.

dishes.name: Typhoon Shelter Crab
dishes.desc: Crab stir-fried with heaps of crispy fried garlic, chili and black beans, created by boat dwellers of Causeway Bay.

dishes.name: French Toast (HK)
dishes.desc: Thick bread slices sandwiched with peanut butter, dipped in egg, deep-fried and served with butter and golden syrup.

dishes.name: Tofu Pudding
dishes.desc: Silky soft tofu served warm with ginger sugar syrup, eaten at Hong Kong dessert shops.

dishes.name: Curry Fish Balls
dishes.desc: Skewered fish balls simmered in a spicy curry sauce, one of Hong Kong's most iconic street snacks.

dishes.name: Macaroni in Soup
dishes.desc: Macaroni in chicken broth with ham strips and often a fried egg, a standard breakfast in Hong Kong cha chaan teng.

dishes.name: Wife Cake
dishes.desc: Flaky round pastry filled with winter melon paste, almond paste and sesame, a traditional Cantonese bakery item.

dishes.name: Baked Pork Chop Rice
dishes.desc: Fried rice topped with a pork chop and tomato sauce, baked under melted cheese.

dishes.name: Cart Noodles
dishes.desc: Noodles with toppings picked from a list, such as fish balls, pig skin and radish, in curry or soy broth.

dishes.name: Minchi
dishes.desc: Macanese minced beef and pork fried with diced potatoes and soy, topped with a fried egg.

dishes.name: Serradura
dishes.desc: Macanese pudding of whipped cream layered with crushed biscuit crumbs.

dishes.name: Dal Bhat
dishes.desc: Steamed rice with lentil soup, vegetable curry, pickles and greens, eaten twice daily across Nepal.

dishes.name: Momo (Nepali)
dishes.desc: Steamed dumplings filled with spiced buffalo, chicken or vegetables, served with tomato-sesame achar.

dishes.name: Sel Roti
dishes.desc: Ring-shaped, slightly sweet rice-flour bread deep-fried in ghee, made especially for Tihar and Dashain.

dishes.name: Newari Khaja Set
dishes.desc: Newar platter of beaten rice with spiced buffalo meat, black soybeans, egg, potatoes and pickles, served at festivals.

dishes.name: Gundruk
dishes.desc: Fermented and dried leafy greens cooked into a sour soup or pickle, considered a national dish of Nepal.

dishes.name: Chatamari
dishes.desc: Thin Newari rice-flour crepe topped with minced meat, egg and spices, often called Newari pizza.

dishes.name: Yomari
dishes.desc: Steamed rice-flour dumpling shaped like a fig and filled with molasses and sesame, made for the Newar Yomari Punhi festival.

dishes.name: Aloo Tama
dishes.desc: Sour curry of potatoes, fermented bamboo shoots and black-eyed beans, a Nepali comfort dish.

dishes.name: Choila
dishes.desc: Newari dish of grilled buffalo meat marinated with mustard oil, chili, garlic and fenugreek, served with beaten rice.

dishes.name: Sekuwa
dishes.desc: Spiced meat chunks skewered and grilled over a wood fire, originating in the hills of eastern Nepal.

dishes.name: Dhido
dishes.desc: Thick porridge of buckwheat, millet or maize flour stirred in boiling water, eaten with curry or gundruk.

dishes.name: Lassi (Nepali)
dishes.desc: Chilled yogurt drink, usually sweet and topped with nuts or cream, sold in Kathmandu and the Terai.

dishes.name: Nepali Milk Tea
dishes.desc: Black tea boiled with milk, sugar and spices such as cardamom and ginger, drunk throughout the day across Nepal.

dishes.name: Juju Dhau
dishes.desc: Sweet, creamy buffalo-milk yogurt set in clay pots, a Bhaktapur speciality known as king curd.

dishes.name: Tongba
dishes.desc: Fermented millet in a wooden vessel topped with hot water, sipped through a bamboo straw.

dishes.name: Sukuti
dishes.desc: Dried spiced buffalo or goat meat, eaten as a snack or tossed into a chilli salad.

dishes.name: Chhurpi
dishes.desc: Hard yak or cow cheese chewed for hours, also made soft for curries.

dishes.name: Tsampa
dishes.desc: Roasted barley flour mixed with butter tea and kneaded into dough balls, the staple food of Tibet.

dishes.name: Butter Tea (Po Cha)
dishes.desc: Brick tea churned with yak butter and salt, drunk many times a day on the Tibetan plateau and in Bhutan.

dishes.name: Ema Datshi
dishes.desc: Bhutanese national dish of hot green or red chilies stewed in melted yak or cow cheese, served with red rice.

dishes.name: Shamdre
dishes.desc: Tibetan dish of rice served with a curry of meat, potatoes, mushrooms and glass noodles, popular at Losar.

dishes.name: Phaksha Paa
dishes.desc: Bhutanese stew of dried pork belly with radish or bok choy and plenty of dried red chilies.

dishes.name: Momos (Tibetan)
dishes.desc: Pleated steamed or fried dumplings filled with yak, beef or vegetables and onion, an everyday and festival food in Tibet.

dishes.name: Thenthuk
dishes.desc: Tibetan soup of hand-pulled flat noodle pieces with mutton or yak, vegetables and spices.

dishes.name: Jasha Maru
dishes.desc: Bhutanese spicy chicken stew with tomatoes, onions, garlic, ginger and chilies, eaten with red rice.

dishes.name: Red Rice
dishes.desc: Semi-milled red rice grown in the Paro valley, cooked as the everyday accompaniment to Bhutanese dishes.

dishes.name: Kewa Datshi
dishes.desc: Bhutanese dish of sliced potatoes simmered with cheese, butter and chilies.

dishes.name: Tingmo
dishes.desc: Fluffy steamed Tibetan bun with spiral layers, eaten with meat stews or dal.

dishes.name: Chang
dishes.desc: Mildly alcoholic home-brewed beer of fermented barley, millet or rice, drunk at Himalayan festivals.

dishes.name: Laphing
dishes.desc: Cold Tibetan mung bean starch noodles dressed with chili oil, garlic, vinegar and soy sauce, a popular street snack.

dishes.name: Shabhaley
dishes.desc: Tibetan fried bread pocket filled with seasoned minced beef or yak and cabbage.

dishes.name: Thukpa
dishes.desc: Hearty Tibetan noodle soup with meat or vegetables, ginger and garlic, popular across Nepal and the Himalaya.

dishes.name: Ara
dishes.desc: Bhutanese rice or millet spirit, often warmed with butter and egg.

dishes.name: Hoentay
dishes.desc: Buckwheat dumplings from the Haa valley filled with turnip greens and cheese.

dishes.name: Nihari
dishes.desc: Slow-cooked beef or mutton shank stew with bone marrow and spices, traditionally eaten for breakfast in Lahore and Karachi.

dishes.name: Haleem
dishes.desc: Thick stew of wheat, barley, lentils and shredded meat cooked for hours, popular during Muharram and Ramadan.

dishes.name: Chapli Kebab
dishes.desc: Flat minced beef patty with tomatoes, pomegranate seeds and coriander, shallow-fried in fat, from Peshawar.

dishes.name: Chicken Karahi
dishes.desc: Chicken cooked in a wok-like karahi with tomatoes, green chilies, ginger and garlic, served with naan.

dishes.name: Sajji
dishes.desc: Whole lamb or chicken stuffed with rice, skewered and slow-roasted around an open fire, a Balochi speciality.

dishes.name: Seekh Kebab
dishes.desc: Spiced minced meat moulded onto long skewers and grilled over charcoal.

dishes.name: Halwa Puri
dishes.desc: Breakfast of deep-fried puri with semolina halwa, chickpea curry and potato curry, especially on Sundays.

dishes.name: Kheer
dishes.desc: Rice pudding slow-cooked in milk with sugar, cardamom and nuts, served at Eid and celebrations.

dishes.name: Biryani (Karachi)
dishes.desc: Layered rice with spicy marinated meat, potatoes, dried plums and yogurt, Karachi's signature biryani style.

dishes.name: Paya
dishes.desc: Goat or cow trotters slow-cooked overnight in a spiced gravy, a winter breakfast dish.

dishes.name: Lahori Fish
dishes.desc: Freshwater fish coated in gram flour batter with ajwain and chili and deep-fried, a Lahore winter street food.

dishes.name: Chana Chaat
dishes.desc: Chickpeas tossed with onion, tomato, chutneys and chaat masala, a tangy snack popular at iftar.

dishes.name: Aloo Paratha
dishes.desc: Whole-wheat flatbread stuffed with spiced mashed potatoes and fried on a griddle with ghee.

dishes.name: Kulfi Falooda
dishes.desc: Dense frozen milk kulfi served with vermicelli, basil seeds and rose syrup.

dishes.name: Gol Gappay
dishes.desc: Crisp hollow puri filled with chickpeas, potatoes and tangy tamarind or spiced water, eaten in one bite.

dishes.name: Pakistani Chai
dishes.desc: Strong black tea boiled with milk and sugar, served at dhabas and homes throughout the day.

dishes.name: Peshawari Namkeen Gosht
dishes.desc: Mutton slow-cooked in its own fat with salt, tomatoes and black pepper, a mildly spiced Peshawar speciality.

dishes.name: Dum Pukht
dishes.desc: Meat and rice sealed in a pot with dough and slow-cooked on low heat, a technique popular in Peshawar.

dishes.name: Lassi (Pakistani)
dishes.desc: Thick yogurt drink served sweet or salted, often topped with cream, a Punjabi summer staple.

dishes.name: Sohan Halwa
dishes.desc: Dense, crunchy sweet of wheat, milk, sugar and ghee studded with nuts, a speciality of Multan.

dishes.name: Bun Kebab
dishes.desc: Bun filled with a fried lentil and meat patty dipped in egg, chutney, onions and raita, Karachi's signature street burger.

dishes.name: Aloo Gosht
dishes.desc: Mutton or beef curry with potatoes, Pakistani everyday cooking.

dishes.name: Shami Kebab
dishes.desc: Pan-fried patties of minced meat and chana dal, served with chutney.

dishes.name: Zarda
dishes.desc: Sweet saffron rice with nuts and raisins, served at weddings.

dishes.name: Noon Chai
dishes.desc: Pink salted Kashmiri tea with milk, topped with crushed pistachios.

dishes.name: Hilsa Curry
dishes.desc: Hilsa fish simmered in a light gravy with turmeric, chili and often potatoes or aubergine.

dishes.name: Kacchi Biryani
dishes.desc: Biryani in which raw marinated mutton and rice are layered and slow-cooked together with potatoes, a Dhaka wedding staple.

dishes.name: Panta Bhat
dishes.desc: Cooked rice soaked overnight in water and lightly fermented, eaten with salt, onion and chili, especially at Pohela Boishakh.

dishes.name: Shatkora Curry
dishes.desc: Sylheti curry of beef or lamb cooked with the rind of the bitter shatkora citrus fruit.

dishes.name: Fuchka
dishes.desc: Crisp hollow shells filled with spiced mashed potatoes, chickpeas and tamarind water, a favourite street snack in Dhaka.

dishes.name: Bhuna Khichuri
dishes.desc: Rice and lentils fried in ghee with spices into a dry khichuri, eaten on rainy days with egg or beef.

dishes.name: Beef Bhuna
dishes.desc: Beef slowly fried with onions and spices until the gravy reduces to a dark, thick coating, popular at Eid.

dishes.name: Shorshe Ilish
dishes.desc: Hilsa fish cooked in a pungent mustard paste with green chilies and mustard oil.

dishes.name: Mishti Doi
dishes.desc: Sweetened yogurt with caramelised sugar set in earthen pots, with the version from Bogra especially famous.

dishes.name: Bakarkhani
dishes.desc: Thick, layered, crisp flatbread baked in a tandoor, an Old Dhaka speciality eaten with tea.

dishes.name: Jhal Muri
dishes.desc: Puffed rice tossed with mustard oil, onions, chilies, peanuts and spices, sold by street vendors.

dishes.name: Chotpoti
dishes.desc: Spicy, tangy dish of yellow peas and potatoes topped with egg, onion, chili and tamarind water.

dishes.name: Pitha
dishes.desc: Rice-flour cakes, steamed, fried or baked and often filled with jaggery and coconut, made especially in winter.

dishes.name: Shutki Bhorta
dishes.desc: Dried fish roasted and mashed with onion, garlic, chili and mustard oil, eaten with rice, especially in Chittagong.

dishes.name: Borhani
dishes.desc: Spiced yogurt drink with mint, coriander and black salt, served with biryani at weddings and feasts.

dishes.name: Rasmalai
dishes.desc: Soft cheese dumplings soaked in sweetened, thickened milk flavoured with cardamom and saffron.

dishes.name: Haji Biryani
dishes.desc: Old Dhaka mutton biryani made with fragrant kalijira rice and mustard oil, made famous by the Haji restaurant since 1939.

dishes.name: Chingri Malai Curry
dishes.desc: Prawns cooked in a mildly spiced coconut milk gravy, a festive Bengali dish.

dishes.name: Dal Puri
dishes.desc: Deep-fried flatbread stuffed with spiced lentil paste, sold as a street snack across Bangladesh.

dishes.name: Roshogolla
dishes.desc: Spongy balls of chhena cheese cooked in light sugar syrup.

dishes.name: Aloo Bhorta
dishes.desc: Mashed potatoes mixed with mustard oil, fried onions, dried chilies and coriander, eaten with rice.

dishes.name: Morog Polao
dishes.desc: Fragrant rice cooked with chicken, ghee, yogurt and whole spices, a favourite at weddings.

dishes.name: Tehari
dishes.desc: Old Dhaka rice dish cooked with beef, mustard oil and green chillies.

dishes.name: Chomchom
dishes.desc: Oval chhena sweet soaked in syrup, famously from Porabari in Tangail.

dishes.name: Kala Bhuna
dishes.desc: Chittagong beef slow-fried with spices until almost black.

dishes.name: Beguni
dishes.desc: Aubergine slices in spiced gram-flour batter, deep-fried for iftar.

dishes.name: Rice and Curry
dishes.desc: Rice served with several curries of vegetables, fish or meat plus sambols and papadums, the everyday Sri Lankan meal.

dishes.name: Kottu Roti
dishes.desc: Chopped godamba roti stir-fried on a griddle with vegetables, egg, meat and curry sauce using clanging metal blades.

dishes.name: Hoppers (Appa)
dishes.desc: Bowl-shaped fermented rice-flour and coconut milk pancakes with crisp edges and soft centres.

dishes.name: String Hoppers
dishes.desc: Steamed nests of rice-flour noodles, eaten for breakfast with curry and pol sambol.

dishes.name: Pol Sambol
dishes.desc: Grated coconut ground with chili, red onion, lime juice and Maldive fish, served with rice and hoppers.

dishes.name: Lamprais
dishes.desc: Burgher dish of rice cooked in stock with mixed meat curry, frikkadels and sambol, baked in a banana leaf.

dishes.name: Kiribath
dishes.desc: Rice cooked in coconut milk and cut into diamonds, served at New Year and auspicious occasions with lunu miris.

dishes.name: Watalappan
dishes.desc: Steamed coconut custard made with kithul jaggery, cardamom and nutmeg, a Sri Lankan Muslim dessert for Eid.

dishes.name: Fish Ambul Thiyal
dishes.desc: Sour, dry fish curry of tuna cooked with goraka, black pepper and spices, a southern coastal speciality.

dishes.name: Egg Hopper
dishes.desc: Bowl-shaped rice-flour hopper with an egg cooked in the centre, eaten with lunu miris chili relish.

dishes.name: Pol Roti
dishes.desc: Griddle-cooked flatbread of wheat flour and grated coconut, often with green chili and onion.

dishes.name: Wambatu Moju
dishes.desc: Sweet and sour pickle of fried aubergine with shallots, green chilies, mustard seeds and vinegar, served with rice.

dishes.name: Ceylon Tea
dishes.desc: Black tea grown in the Sri Lankan highlands, drunk strong with milk and sugar throughout the day.

dishes.name: Gotu Kola Sambol
dishes.desc: Finely chopped pennywort leaves mixed with grated coconut, shallots, lime and chili, served as a fresh side.

dishes.name: Short Eats
dishes.desc: Assorted savoury snacks such as fish buns, patties, rolls and cutlets, sold in bakeries and tea shops.

dishes.name: Kokis
dishes.desc: Crisp, deep-fried rosette-shaped cookie of rice flour and coconut milk, made for Sinhala and Tamil New Year.

dishes.name: Mas Huni
dishes.desc: Maldivian breakfast of shredded smoked tuna with grated coconut, onion and chili, eaten with roshi flatbread.

dishes.name: Garudhiya
dishes.desc: Clear Maldivian tuna broth eaten with rice, lime, chili and onions.

dishes.name: Bis Keemiya
dishes.desc: Maldivian fried pastry filled with cabbage, boiled egg and onion, a common short eat at tea shops.

dishes.name: Curd and Treacle
dishes.desc: Thick buffalo-milk curd set in clay pots and drizzled with kithul palm treacle, a southern Sri Lankan dessert.

dishes.name: Parippu
dishes.desc: Red lentils cooked in coconut milk with turmeric, curry leaves and tempered spices, served with almost every rice and curry meal.

dishes.name: Isso Vadai
dishes.desc: Crisp fried lentil fritters topped with whole prawns, sold from beachside carts on Galle Face Green.

dishes.name: Pittu
dishes.desc: Steamed cylinders of rice flour and grated coconut, eaten with curry or coconut milk.

dishes.name: Kavum
dishes.desc: Deep-fried oil cake of rice flour and treacle, made for Sinhala and Tamil New Year.

dishes.name: Arrack
dishes.desc: Spirit distilled from coconut palm sap, mixed with ginger beer.

dishes.name: Jaffna Crab Curry
dishes.desc: Northern Sri Lankan crab curry with roasted Jaffna curry powder and murunga leaves.

dishes.name: Nasi Goreng
dishes.desc: Fried rice seasoned with sweet soy sauce, shallots, garlic and chili, often topped with a fried egg and krupuk.

dishes.name: Gado-Gado
dishes.desc: Salad of blanched vegetables, tofu, tempeh, egg and potatoes dressed with peanut sauce.

dishes.name: Soto Ayam
dishes.desc: Turmeric-yellow chicken soup with vermicelli, boiled egg, bean sprouts and fried shallots.

dishes.name: Bakso
dishes.desc: Beef meatball soup with noodles, tofu and fried shallots, sold from street carts.

dishes.name: Mie Goreng
dishes.desc: Stir-fried yellow noodles with sweet soy sauce, garlic, vegetables and egg, topped with fried shallots.

dishes.name: Ayam Penyet
dishes.desc: Fried chicken smashed with a pestle and served with fiery sambal, rice, tofu and tempeh.

dishes.name: Tempeh
dishes.desc: Fermented soybean cake from Java, fried, braised or grilled and eaten as a protein-rich side.

dishes.name: Martabak
dishes.desc: Pan-fried stuffed pancake, either savoury with egg and minced meat or thick and sweet with chocolate and cheese.

dishes.name: Es Cendol
dishes.desc: Iced drink of green pandan rice-flour jelly with coconut milk and palm sugar syrup.

dishes.name: Babi Guling
dishes.desc: Balinese whole suckling pig stuffed with spice paste and spit-roasted, served with lawar and rice.

dishes.name: Gudeg
dishes.desc: Young jackfruit stewed for hours with palm sugar and coconut milk, a Yogyakarta speciality served with chicken and egg.

dishes.name: Rawon
dishes.desc: Dark beef soup from East Java coloured black by keluak nuts, served with rice and salted egg.

dishes.name: Sate Ayam
dishes.desc: Grilled chicken skewers served with peanut sauce, sweet soy and rice cakes, sold by street vendors.

dishes.name: Bebek Betutu
dishes.desc: Balinese duck rubbed with spice paste, wrapped in banana leaves and slow-cooked, served at ceremonies.

dishes.name: Nasi Campur
dishes.desc: Rice served with small portions of meats, vegetables, peanuts, eggs and sambal, varying from island to island.

dishes.name: Lumpia Semarang
dishes.desc: Spring rolls filled with bamboo shoots, egg and shrimp or chicken, a speciality of Semarang.

dishes.name: Soto Betawi
dishes.desc: Jakarta beef and offal soup in a coconut milk and milk broth with tomato and potato, topped with emping crackers.

dishes.name: Ketoprak
dishes.desc: Jakarta street dish of tofu, rice cakes, vermicelli and bean sprouts in peanut sauce with sweet soy.

dishes.name: Klepon
dishes.desc: Green glutinous rice balls filled with liquid palm sugar and rolled in grated coconut.

dishes.name: Bubur Ayam
dishes.desc: Rice congee topped with shredded chicken, fried shallots, soy sauce and crackers, a common breakfast.

dishes.name: Opor Ayam
dishes.desc: Chicken braised in a mild coconut milk curry, served with ketupat rice cakes during Lebaran.

dishes.name: Nasi Uduk
dishes.desc: Betawi rice cooked in coconut milk and lemongrass, served with fried chicken, tempeh, egg and sambal.

dishes.name: Siomay
dishes.desc: Steamed fish dumplings with tofu, potato and cabbage, served with peanut sauce, a Bandung street food.

dishes.name: Tumpeng
dishes.desc: Cone-shaped mound of yellow rice surrounded by side dishes, served at Javanese celebrations.

dishes.name: Sambal Matah
dishes.desc: Raw Balinese relish of sliced shallots, lemongrass, chilies, lime leaves and coconut oil.

dishes.name: Sate Lilit
dishes.desc: Balinese minced fish with coconut and spices wrapped around lemongrass sticks and grilled.

dishes.name: Lawar
dishes.desc: Balinese mix of minced meat, grated coconut, vegetables and spices.

dishes.name: Sop Buntut
dishes.desc: Clear oxtail soup with carrots, potatoes and fried shallots.

dishes.name: Rujak
dishes.desc: Fruit salad with a spicy palm-sugar, tamarind and chilli dressing.

dishes.name: Es Teler
dishes.desc: Iced dessert of avocado, young coconut and jackfruit in coconut milk and condensed milk.

dishes.name: Pecel Lele
dishes.desc: Fried catfish with sambal, raw vegetables and rice from roadside tents.

dishes.name: Nasi Liwet
dishes.desc: Javanese rice cooked in coconut milk and chicken broth, served with side dishes.

dishes.name: Mie Ayam
dishes.desc: Noodles topped with sweet-soy diced chicken and bok choy, with broth on the side.

dishes.name: Rendang
dishes.desc: Minangkabau dish of beef slow-cooked in coconut milk and spice paste until dry and caramelised.

dishes.name: Nasi Padang

dishes.name: Buuz
dishes.desc: Steamed dumplings filled with minced mutton and onion, made by the hundreds for Tsagaan Sar.

dishes.name: Khuushuur
dishes.desc: Fried flat pastries filled with mutton, eaten especially during the Naadam festival.

dishes.name: Tsuivan
dishes.desc: Stir-fried hand-cut noodles with mutton, cabbage, carrots and onions, a staple Mongolian home meal.

dishes.name: Khorkhog
dishes.desc: Mutton cooked with hot stones in a sealed pot with vegetables, served at gatherings in the countryside.

dishes.name: Airag
dishes.desc: Fermented mare's milk, slightly alcoholic, the traditional drink of summer and Naadam.

dishes.name: Boortsog
dishes.desc: Fried dough cookies served with milk tea and at celebrations.

dishes.name: Bantan
dishes.desc: Thick soup of flour crumbs and minced meat, eaten as comfort food or when sick.

dishes.name: Suutei Tsai (Milk Tea)
dishes.desc: Salted milk tea of green tea boiled with milk and water, sometimes with butter or rice.

dishes.name: Ul Boov
dishes.desc: Stacked layers of fried shoe-sole cakes with dairy sweets, the centrepiece of the Tsagaan Sar table.

dishes.name: Bansh
dishes.desc: Small meat dumplings boiled in water, broth or milk tea.

dishes.name: Guriltai Shul
dishes.desc: Hearty soup of hand-cut noodles with mutton, potatoes and carrots, an everyday meal in Mongolian homes.

dishes.name: Aaruul
dishes.desc: Curds dried in the sun on ger roofs into hard, sour pieces, eaten as a snack all year.

dishes.name: Boodog
dishes.desc: Whole goat or marmot cooked from the inside with hot stones placed in the skin and blowtorched outside.

dishes.name: Budaatai Khuurga
dishes.desc: Rice stir-fried with mutton or beef, carrots and onions, an everyday Mongolian canteen dish.

dishes.name: Byaslag
dishes.desc: Mild pressed cheese of cow or yak milk, sliced and eaten with tea or dried for winter.

dishes.name: Gambir
dishes.desc: Flaky Mongolian pan-fried pancake of layered dough, eaten plain or with sugar and clotted cream.

dishes.name: Urum
dishes.desc: Thick clotted cream skimmed from boiled milk, eaten with bread and sugar.
